items.title: Section: Three Places Where Mindfulness Is Lost — Amid Sense Objects, Across Successive Rebirths, and Regarding What Was Once Learned

items.zh: 於其三處有忘失念。一、於境界可意、不可意色聲香味觸法中，或於一時其心顛倒，忘失正念；二、於受生彼彼身中，既受生已，忘失前生；三、於所受、所持諸法，久作久說，或於一時有所忘失。於是三處有忘失念。
items.en:
There are three places where this bodhisattva loses correct mindfulness. First, amid pleasant and unpleasant sights, sounds, smells, tastes, textures, and mental objects, at times the mind becomes distorted, correct mindfulness lost. Second, having taken rebirth in this or that body, once reborn, the previous life is forgotten. Third, regarding teachings once received and retained, long practised and long expounded, at times these are simply forgotten.
These are the three places where this bodhisattva loses correct mindfulness.

items.title: Section: Intelligence and Memory That Come and Go, and Teaching Others Only Through Strained, Uncertain Effort — Like Shooting an Arrow in the Dark

items.zh: 或於一時具足聰慧，於其諸法能受、能持，於其義理堪能悟入，或於一時則不如是。或於一時具足憶念，或於一時成忘念類。於諸有情未能了知如實調伏善巧方便，於自佛法亦未了知如實引發善巧方便。為他說法教授教誡，勉勵而轉；勉勵轉故，不如實知，或時虛棄、或不虛棄。如闇中射，或中不中，隨欲成故。
items.en:
At times such a bodhisattva possesses genuine intelligence, able to receive and retain the teaching, capable of penetrating its meaning; at other times this is not the case.
At times such a bodhisattva possesses genuine retentive memory; at other times forgetfulness prevails instead.
Not yet genuinely, correctly knowing the skilful means for taming sentient beings, and not yet genuinely, correctly knowing the skilful means for drawing forth one's own buddha-teaching, such a bodhisattva, in instructing and admonishing others through teaching the true teaching, proceeds only through strained exertion; because it proceeds through strained exertion, it does not genuinely, correctly know its own effect — at times accomplishing nothing, at times not accomplishing nothing. It is like shooting an arrow in darkness, sometimes striking and sometimes missing, because it proceeds in accordance with desire.
Commentary: Regarding "because it proceeds in accordance with desire" — because such a bodhisattva's own aspiration is not yet pure, this is precisely why such a shortcoming occurs, one should understand.

items.title: Section: Six Ways Attainment Can Still Regress — Abandoning Bodhicitta, Giving Back the Precepts, Wearying of Beings, Repeated Violation, Fearing the Great Vehicle, and Losing Great Compassion

items.zh: 或於一時，於大菩提雖已發心，而復退捨。或於一時，棄捨菩薩先所受學淨戒律儀，不能受學。或於一時，雖勤修習利有情事，而於中間生厭倦故，復還棄捨利有情事。由意樂故，欲令自樂；由思擇故，欲令他樂。於諸菩薩所有違犯，多分遍知，非數遍知、無餘永斷，由於毀犯數現行故。或於一時，於菩薩藏法毘奈耶他所引奪。或於一時，聞說甚深廣大法教而生驚怖，其心搖動、猶豫、疑惑。於諸有情，遠離一切現行大悲。於諸有情，少分現前利益安樂，未能廣大、未能無量。
items.en:
At times, though the aspiration for great awakening has already been aroused, it is abandoned and relinquished after all.
At times, such a bodhisattva even discards the pure precept-discipline of a bodhisattva already received, no longer able to sustain it.
At times, though diligently cultivating what benefits sentient beings, midway through, weariness and discouragement arise, and the work of benefiting beings is abandoned once again. Out of this aspiration, one wishes to secure one's own ease; only through deliberate reflection does one again wish to bring others ease.
With respect to every possible violation among the bodhisattva precepts, such a bodhisattva mostly, but not completely, knows them, and has not yet entirely and permanently eliminated them, which is why repeated violation still occurs.
At times, such a bodhisattva's own grasp of the bodhisattva canon's teaching and discipline is overtaken by rival forces. At times, upon hearing the profound, vast teachings expounded, genuine terror arises, the mind wavering, hesitant, and doubtful.
Such a bodhisattva remains far from all continuous display of great compassion towards sentient beings. Towards sentient beings, only a small portion can be wished immediate benefit and ease — not yet vast, not yet boundless.

items.title: Section: Not Yet Fully Learned, Not Yet Fully Manifested, Feeling Far From Awakening — Closing the Full Account of This Abode's Conduct, State, and Mark

items.zh: 於如上說一切圓滿菩薩學中，未能普學。於如上說一切圓滿菩薩諸相，未皆成就。於如上說一切圓滿二分菩薩正加行中，未等顯現。於如上說菩薩意樂，猶未清淨。於其無上正等菩提，自謂為遠，未於涅槃增上意樂安立深固。如於生死長時流轉，於其熾然、無動、妙善菩提分法，未能成就。如是等類，當知是名勝解行住菩薩轉時，諸行狀相。
items.en:
Within all the complete bodhisattva training already explained above, such a bodhisattva has not yet universally mastered it. Within all the complete marks of a bodhisattva already explained above, such a bodhisattva has not yet accomplished them all. Within all the complete applied efforts of both divisions of bodhisattva already explained above, such a bodhisattva has not yet manifested them equally. The excellent aspiration of a bodhisattva already explained above remains, for such a bodhisattva, not yet purified.
Towards unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening, such a bodhisattva regards it as far away, not yet having established a deep, firm excellent aspiration towards nirvana. Correspondingly caught in the long circulation of birth-and-death, such a bodhisattva has not yet accomplished the blazing, unshakeable, wondrously excellent factors of awakening.
All of this together, one should understand, is called the conduct, state, and mark of a bodhisattva turning within the abode of resolute practice.
Commentary: Regarding "correspondingly caught in the long circulation of birth-and-death" and the like — because such a bodhisattva may still go to an unfortunate rebirth, this is why it is said to be a long circulation. One should understand that such a bodhisattva has not yet become joined with any of these blazing, unshakeable, utterly pure factors of awakening whatsoever, exactly as explained in the Chapter on Maturation. This should be understood accordingly.

items.title: Section: Three Grades Within Resolute Practice Itself, and the Seamless, Instantaneous Transition Into Utmost Joy

items.zh: 是諸菩薩勝解行住，下忍轉時，如上所說諸行狀相，當知上品；中忍轉時，如上所說諸行狀相，當知中品；上忍轉時，如上所說，當知下品，其性微薄。即於如是上忍轉時，於上所說諸行狀相，漸次能令無餘永斷，從此無間，當知菩薩入極喜住。
items.en:
Bodhisattvas at the abode of resolute practice, when turning at the stage of lower forbearance, should be understood, with respect to the conduct, state, and mark already explained above, to be at the superior grade; when turning at the stage of middling forbearance, should be understood to be at the middling grade; when turning at the stage of superior forbearance, should be understood to be at the inferior grade, their underlying nature having grown faint and thin.
Precisely at this stage of superior forbearance, with respect to the conduct, state, and mark already explained above, these are gradually, completely severed without remainder, and from this point, without any interval, one should understand that such a bodhisattva enters the abode of utmost joy.

items.title: Section: Defiled Versus Pure, and Why Resolute Practice Still Cannot Be Called Excellent Aspiration — Closing the Abode of Resolute Practice Entirely

items.zh: 由得方便極喜住中，勝解行住所說諸法皆無所有，與彼相違所有一切白品諸法皆悉顯現。由諸菩薩成就此故，轉得名為淨勝意樂。勝解行住菩薩轉時，雖有少分軟中上品方便展轉清淨勝解，而未得名淨勝意樂。何以故？由此勝解為彼多種諸隨煩惱染污而轉。極歡喜住菩薩住時，一切勝解諸隨煩惱皆悉永斷，離隨煩惱淨勝解轉。
items.en:
Because a bodhisattva has attained the skilful means present within the abode of utmost joy, none of the dharmas already explained under the abode of resolute practice are present at all — instead, every contrary wholesome quality manifests fully. Because such bodhisattvas accomplish this, they turn and come to be called ones of pure, excellent aspiration.
When a bodhisattva at the abode of resolute practice turns, although there is a small portion of gradually purifying resolute understanding at the lesser, middling, or superior grade, this still cannot be called pure, excellent aspiration. Why is this? Because this resolute understanding turns defiled by numerous secondary afflictions.
When a bodhisattva abiding in the abode of utmost joy turns, all secondary afflictions connected with resolute understanding are permanently and forever cut off, and, free of secondary affliction, one turns with pure resolute understanding.
Commentary: Regarding "turns defiled by numerous secondary afflictions" — the chapter on the lineage explains: there are four secondary afflictions contrary to wholesome dharmas, called the numerous secondary afflictions. Whether complete or incomplete, being defiled by them is called turning defiled. The four secondary afflictions should be understood exactly as listed there (fascicle 35, page 2845 of the Nanjing edition).

items.title: Section: The Abode of Utmost Joy Opens — An Eightfold Question, and the First Mark of Well-Determined Vow

items.zh: 問：極歡喜住菩薩轉時，應知何行、何狀、何相？答：若諸菩薩，從勝解行住入極歡喜住，先於無上正等菩提菩薩弘願，未善通達菩提自性，未善通達菩提方便，多分隨順他緣而轉，不善決定。除捨彼故，發起六相新善決定、內證修性菩薩大願。

items.title: Section: The Remaining Three Marks — Peerless, Uncommon, Unchanging-Inexhaustible — Closing the Well-Determined Vow Entirely

items.zh: 超過一切餘白淨願；無等不共，果是世間，超過一切世間境界；隨救一切有情苦故，不共一切聲聞、獨覺；雖一剎那生起此願，法性自爾能得菩薩無量白法可愛之果；又此大願無變無盡自性得已，無異因緣令其退轉、變異可得；又是勝分，墮後邊際極大菩提。如此菩薩善決定願，亦名發心。
items.en:
This vow of realising dharma-nature directly surpasses every other wholesome, pure vow. Peerless and uncommon: its fruit, though worldly, surpasses every worldly object entirely; because one vows to follow and rescue every sentient being's suffering, it is uncommon to any hearer or solitary-realiser. Even arising for a single instant, this vow, by its own nature, spontaneously secures the bodhisattva immeasurable, cherished wholesome fruits.
Furthermore, once this great vow's unchanging, inexhaustible own-nature is attained, no other cause or condition whatsoever can bring about its regression or alteration. Furthermore, this is the excellent portion, assured of eventually reaching the furthest boundary, the greatest awakening.
Such a bodhisattva's well-determined vow may also be called the arising of bodhicitta.

blocks.text: The portrait of the not-yet-noble bodhisattva continues, then the first ground, utmost joy, opens with the "well-determined vow".

Master Cháng Bǎi: people living together are like potatoes being washed, bumping into each other, afflictions arising constantly. Venerable Miào Jìng: the mind cannot yet turn towards ultimate truth; it grasps and clings.

Venerable Miào Jìng: one's practice is careless and one's teaching unreliable. Master Cháng Bǎi: like shooting arrows in the dark, hitting the target is luck; sometimes it is said in vain, only planting a distant seed.
Venerable Miào Jìng: affliction takes charge, wisdom cannot, so they stop studying; hearing profound teaching they say, "Oh, is that so? Can I do it?" They have no confidence in themselves.
Venerable Miào Jìng: middle forbearance corresponds to the stages of heat and summit. Master Cháng Bǎi: at lower forbearance the flaws are strong and obvious; at upper forbearance they are faint.
"Because that conviction operates stained by many secondary afflictions." Master Cháng Bǎi names four: heedlessness, wrong view, distraction, and obstruction.
Venerable Miào Jìng: awakening's nature is the fruit; awakening's means are the cause. Master Cháng Bǎi: awakening's nature is the two eliminations and the two wisdoms.

"This bodhisattva's well-determined vow is also called arousing the mind." Master Cháng Bǎi: it is arousing ultimate bodhicitta. Venerable Miào Jìng: not abandoning birth and death is great compassion; not being stained by it is great wisdom.

Master Cháng Bǎi's potatoes are memorable: among other people, we knock against one another and afflictions arise constantly. Mindfulness is easiest to lose there, which is exactly where it is most needed.

quiz.q: For the first place mindfulness is lost — amid pleasant and unpleasant objects — what image does Master Cháng Bǎi use?
options: living together like potatoes being washed — bumping, constant afflictions
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: people living together are like potatoes being washed — bumping into each other, afflictions arising constantly. Venerable Miào Jìng: the mind can't turn towards ultimate truth; it grasps and clings.

quiz.q: Teaching "like shooting in the dark — hit or miss, 隨欲成故." The English renders 隨欲 as chance. How do the lectures read it?
options: Miào Jìng: careless practice and unreliable teaching — tied to impure intention; Cháng Bǎi: shooting in the dark is pure luck — sometimes it's wasted breath, merely sowing a distant seed
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: one's practice is careless and one's teaching unreliable. Master Cháng Bǎi: like shooting arrows in the dark — hitting the target is pure luck; sometimes it's said in vain, only planting a distant seed. The commentary and Miào Jìng tie 欲 to still-impure intention.

quiz.q: "Pulled away from the bodhisattva canon by others" — the English note says by outsiders. How does Venerable Miào Jìng read it?
options: afflictions take charge; wisdom can't, so they stop learning
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: affliction takes charge, wisdom can't, so they stop studying; hearing profound teaching: "Oh — is that so? Can I do it?" — no confidence in themselves.

quiz.q: Faults are "superior at lower forbearance, inferior at superior forbearance." How do the lectures map these stages?
options: Miào Jìng: the ten faiths are outer-ordinary; middle forbearance is heat and summit; Cháng Bǎi: at lower forbearance faults are strong ("superior grade"), heat and summit are middle, at upper forbearance faults are faint
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the ten faiths are outer-ordinary; middle forbearance corresponds to heat and summit. Master Cháng Bǎi: at lower forbearance the flawed states are strong and obvious — "superior grade"; entering heat and summit is middle forbearance; at upper forbearance faults are faint.

quiz.q: Why does the resolute-practice abode, despite some pure conviction, not count as "pure excellent aspiration"?
options: that conviction still operates stained by many secondary afflictions
quiz.why: "Because that conviction operates stained by many secondary afflictions." Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary bodhisattvas have four — heedlessness, wrong view, distraction, and obstruction.

quiz.q: Before utmost joy, the bodhisattva "hadn't penetrated awakening's nature or its means." How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish them?
options: awakening's nature is the fruit; its means the cause
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: awakening's nature is the fruit; awakening's means are the cause. Master Cháng Bǎi: awakening's nature is the two eliminations and two wisdoms; previously one mostly followed others' conditions.

quiz.q: The treatise says this well-determined vow is "also called" what?
quiz.why: "This bodhisattva's well-determined vow is also called arousing the mind." Master Cháng Bǎi: it is arousing ultimate bodhicitta.

quiz.q: The vow is "uncommon to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas." How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe the bodhisattva's compassion and wisdom?
options: not abandoning saṃsāra is great compassion; not being stained by it is great wisdom
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: not abandoning birth and death is great compassion; not being stained by it is great wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: uncommon to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas who don't vow to return life after life.
